name: containerize-aspnet-framework
description: Containerize an ASP.NET .NET Framework project for Windows Docker by creating customized Dockerfile and .dockerignore files.

Containerize the project specified below, focusing **exclusively** on changes required for the application to run in a Windows Docker container. This is a .NET Framework application, not .NET Core.

Settings (unspecified values use defaults):
- Project: `[ProjectName (provide path to .csproj file)]`
- Windows Server SKU: `[Windows Server Core (Default) or Windows Server Full]`
- Windows Server version: `[2016, 2019, or 2022]`
- Build base image: `[Specify base image to use for build stage (Default None)]`
- Run base image: `[Specify base image to use for run stage (Default None)]`
- Ports: Primary HTTP `[e.g., 80]`; additional `[List any additional ports, or "None"]`
- User: `[User account, or default to "ContainerUser"]`
- IIS settings: `[List any specific IIS settings, or "None"]`
- Pre/post-build steps: `[List any specific build steps, or "None"]`
- GAC assemblies, MSIs, COM: `[Assembly name and version, or "None"]`; `[MSI names and versions, or "None"]`; `[COM component names, or "None"]`
- Registry, environment, roles/features: `[Registry paths and values, or "None"]`; `[Variable names and values, or "Use defaults"]`; `[Role/feature names, or "None"]`
- Files to copy and target: `[Paths relative to project root, or "None"]`; `[Container paths, or "Not applicable"]`
- Exclusions: `[Paths to exclude, or "None"]`
- Additional `.dockerignore` patterns: `[List any additional patterns, or "None"]`
- Health check endpoint and interval/timeout: `[Health check URL path, or "None"]`; `[Interval and timeout values, or "Use defaults"]`
- Other instructions and known issues: `[Specific requirements, or "None"]`; `[Describe any known issues, or "None"]`

✅ App configuration modification to ensure config builders are used to read app settings and connection strings from the environment variables  
✅ Dockerfile creation and configuration for an ASP.NET application  
✅ Specifying multiple stages in the Dockerfile to build/publish the application and copy the output to the final image  
✅ Configuration of Windows container platform compatibility (Windows Server Core or Full)  
✅ Proper handling of dependencies (GAC assemblies, MSIs, COM components)  
❌ No infrastructure setup (assumed to be handled separately)  
❌ No code changes beyond those required for containerization  

Procedure:
1. Review the containerization settings above to understand the containerization requirements.
2. Create a `progress.md` file to track changes with check marks.
3. Determine the .NET Framework version from the project's .csproj file by checking the `TargetFrameworkVersion` element.
4. Select the appropriate Windows Server image using the detected .NET Framework version, SKU, and version (2016, 2019, or 2022). Windows Server Core tags: https://github.com/microsoft/dotnet-framework-docker/blob/main/README.aspnet.md#full-tag-listing
5. Ensure that required NuGet packages are installed. **DO NOT** install these if they are missing. If they are not installed, the user must install them manually. If they are not installed, pause executing this prompt and ask the user to install them using the Visual Studio NuGet Package Manager or Visual Studio package manager console. Required package: `Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment`.
6. Modify `web.config`:
   - Add ConfigBuilders section in configSections.
   - Add configBuilders section in the root.
   - Configure EnvironmentConfigBuilder for both appSettings and connectionStrings:
```xml
<section name="configBuilders" type="System.Configuration.ConfigurationBuildersSection, System.Configuration, Version=<REDACTED_IP>, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a" restartOnExternalChanges="false" requirePermission="false" />
<add name="Environment" type="Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.EnvironmentConfigBuilder, Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment" />
<appSettings configBuilders="Environment">
<!-- existing app settings -->
<connectionStrings configBuilders="Environment">
<!-- existing connection strings -->
```
7. Create a `LogMonitorConfig.json` file in the folder where the Dockerfile will be created by copying the reference `LogMonitorConfig.json` file at the end of this prompt. The file's contents **MUST NOT** not be modified and should match the reference content exactly unless instructions in containerization settings specify otherwise. Do not change the issue level to `Information` for EventLog sources.
8. Create a Dockerfile in the root of the project directory:
   - Use multiple stages. The build stage MUST use a `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/sdk` base image unless a custom base image is specified in the settings file.
   - Copy sln, csproj, and packages.config files first; copy NuGet.config if it exists and configure private feeds; restore NuGet packages; copy remaining source; build/publish to `C:\publish` using MSBuild.
   - The final stage MUST use a `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/aspnet` base image unless a custom base image is specified in the settings file.
   - Copy `LogMonitorConfig.json` to a container directory such as `C:\LogMonitor`; download LogMonitor.exe there from https://github.com/microsoft/windows-container-tools/releases/download/v2.1.1/LogMonitor.exe.
   - Set working directory to `C:\inetpub\wwwroot`; copy `C:\publish`; apply user, IIS, GAC, MSI, COM, roles/features, registry, environment, and file requirements.
   - Set entry point exactly:
`ENTRYPOINT [ "C:\\LogMonitor\\LogMonitor.exe", "C:\\ServiceMonitor.exe", "w3svc" ]`
   - **IMPORTANT:** Use a Windows Server Core base image unless the user has **specifically requested** a full Windows Server image in the settings file
9. Create a `.dockerignore` file in the root of the project directory. It MUST include common defaults and all additional configured patterns.
10. If a health check endpoint is provided, add a HEALTHCHECK instruction.
11. Add the dockerfile to the project by adding the following item to the project file: `<None Include="Dockerfile" />`
12. Mark tasks as completed: [ ] → [✓]
13. Continue until all tasks are complete and Docker build succeeds. Use the following command:
`docker build
